title: Polaris weekly units-per-dollar POC sync
summary: Weekly POC check-in focused on units-per-dollar metrics. Reviewed benchmarking results (tokens/sec/$), caching and batching adjustments, and next steps: run 48h production-style bench, enable prefix caching for high-hit paths, tweak batching window, and share pricing/security docs.
action_items: Samir: send updated benchmark spreadsheet + pricing worksheet (due 2026-02-19)
Jules: enable prefix cache on dev cluster and run 24h replay (due 2026-02-20)
Diego: provide 5 representative production prompt traces to Redwood (due 2026-02-19)
Aisha: confirm required encryption/KMS controls and share firewall diagram (due 2026-02-24)
next_steps: Redwood to run a 48h tokens-per-dollar benchmark with production prompt set
Polaris to share target latency SLOs and production prompt distribution
Schedule follow-up sync next Tuesday to review 48h results
Samir to send SOC2 + ISO + KMS checklist and pricing tiers
transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-02-18 16:00 UTC - Duration 54 minutes
Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Jules Huang (Redwood SE), Melissa Cole (Polaris CTO), Diego Rivera (ML Engineer), Aisha Khan (SRE)

[00:00] Samir (Redwood): okay everyone thanks for joining, quick agenda — results from last week's run, caching/batching tweaks we applied, cost per unit numbers and next steps. Melissa, you had a hard stop at 5:00pm?
[00:12] Melissa (Polaris): yeah roughly 45 minutes, that's fine.
[00:18] Jules (Redwood SE): hi all, I pulled the numbers into the sheet Samir shared. there are a couple of anomalies but overall the tokens per dollar improved after we turned on prefix caching for the 3 main routes.
[00:32] Diego (Polaris): quick question, when you say prefix caching is on, is that the KV cache or like a separate prefix-level cache? sometimes our logs call it K V cash so i want to align.
[00:40] Jules (Redwood SE): good point — it's the prefix cache (we use a lightweight KV cache for prefix keys). on the dev cluster we observed about a 28% token cost reduction on chat-history dominated flows where prefixes repeat.
[00:55] Aisha (Polaris SRE): and that was with the same quantization profile? we saw you suggested int8, right?
[01:02] Samir (Redwood): yes we tested int8 and int4 options. the main 48h sample that Jules ran used int8 quantization for the longest sequences to keep quality stable; int4 gave slightly better cost but some quality regressions on the 2-shot prompts.
[01:18] Melissa (Polaris CTO): can you summarize tokens per dollar numbers? our CFO keeps asking for tokens per dollar and tokens per second per dollar — she's mixing metrics.
[01:26] Jules (Redwood SE): sure. baseline hosted model (no caching, small batch window) was about 2.5k tokens / $ on our test profile. after prefix caching + batching window 30ms we measured ~3.4k tokens / $. with dedicated GPU + larger batching (75ms) we hit ~5.1k tokens / $. numbers are noisy — they vary by sequence length distribution.
[01:50] Diego (Polaris ML): that delta seems big — is the improvement mostly due to batching or the dedicated instance efficiency?
[01:58] Jules (Redwood SE): both. batching improves throughput by increasing token concurrency; dedicated has lower scheduling overhead and more aggressive kernel selection, so per-token compute cost drops. caching reduces repeated token generation altogether.
[02:12] Melissa (Polaris CTO): what's the tail latency impact? our product requires 95th percentile < 400ms for interactive flows.
[02:19] Jules (Redwood SE): with batching at 75ms we saw average latency increase by ~60ms but p95 stayed around 420-480ms — so slightly above your SLO. at 30ms batching p95 was ~360ms but tokens/sec/$ lower than the 75ms config. it's the classic latency vs cost tradeoff.
[02:40] Samir (Redwood): right — you can think of it as two levers: batching window and routing to dedicated vs hosted. we also have the option to do mixed routing: route high-priority interactive requests to low-latency pool and batch background inference into the cost-optimized pool.
[02:58] Aisha (Polaris SRE): do you support policy-based routing? say route by route name or by header?
[03:04] Jules (Redwood SE): yes, header-based routing is supported; you can tag requests as "interactive" and they hit the low-latency nodes. that reduces cost-efficiency somewhat but keeps SLOs.
[03:18] Melissa (Polaris CTO): what's the expected budget delta if we do mixed routing: like 70% interactive, 30% background?
[03:27] Jules (Redwood SE): ballpark: if you keep 70% traffic in low-latency pool (higher cost), overall tokens/$ drops to ~3.0k tokens / $. shifting 30% background into optimized pool recovers some — it's basically weighted average. we'll run the 48h run with your real traffic profile to get better numbers.
[03:45] Diego (Polaris ML): on caching: we saw hit rate around 45% on two routes, but other routes are low. can we do partial prefix caching — like only cache system prompts or stable prefaces?
[03:58] Jules (Redwood SE): absolutely — prefix cache is configurable per route or prompt key. a lot of customers cache system messages + user profiles, not raw user queries. that yields the biggest wins without hurting personalization.
[04:14] Melissa (Polaris CTO): security question — any concerns with caching sensitive PII in the cache? we need encryption + TTL controls.
[04:22] Samir (Redwood): yes, we support encrypted at-rest caches, per-customer KMS integration, and TTL/eviction policies. we can also configure cache to avoid storing any keys flagged as PII. Jules, remind them about audit logs.
[04:35] Jules (Redwood SE): audit logs are available — who hit cache, miss rates, evictions. also access is RBAC controlled via SSO/SAML integration.
[04:44] Aisha (Polaris SRE): good. for on-prem or VPC deployments, does Redwood Private support customer-managed HSM?
[04:51] Samir (Redwood): yes — Private supports HSM/KMS, and there's an on-prem package for full air-gapped setups. we'll include the cert matrix in the docs Samir sends.
[05:02] Melissa (Polaris CTO): ok. can we dig into the benchmark anomalies you mentioned?
[05:08] Jules (Redwood SE): sure — there was a spike on day 2 of the run where tokens/sec/$ dropped by 12% for about three hours. logs show a scheduling back-off on the serving cluster caused by a transient backlog — we mitigated by adjusting autoscaling thresholds. it's the reason we want a longer run with production traces.
[05:28] Diego (Polaris ML): autoscaling thresholds meaning? you changed the queue depth trigger?
[05:33] Jules (Redwood SE): correct — increased the queue depth trigger and lowered cold-start concurrency limits to avoid backpressure. it's subtle but matters for cost numbers when traffic has bursts.
[05:46] Melissa (Polaris CTO): I want a conservative number to share with finance. can you give a lower-bound estimate for tokens per dollar we can guarantee for the POC?
[05:55] Samir (Redwood): for the POC we'll give a conservative baseline of 2.8k tokens / $ for hosted with caching + 3.8k tokens / $ for dedicated with caching, both assuming your current prompt distribution. Final numbers will come from the 48h replay.
[06:10] Aisha (Polaris SRE): about batching windows: what's the impact on CPU/GPU utilization? we saw GPUs saturating during the 75ms batching runs.
[06:19] Jules (Redwood SE): larger windows increase sustained GPU utilization (good for throughput) but can hit memory limits for very long sequences (KV cache growth). we've got a telemetry alert template to avoid OOMs — we'll share.
[06:30] Speaker 6: (background) mm-hmm
[06:33] Diego (Polaris ML): quality checks — when you quantize more aggressively, how do you recommend validating regressions? we have an eval harness but need guidance.
[06:41] Jules (Redwood SE): we recommend a two-track eval: synthetic holdout + business prompt set. track token-level divergence and downstream task A/B — provide regression thresholds and automatic rollback to higher-precision model. Redwood Optimize can suggest quant profiles per workload.
[06:58] Melissa (Polaris CTO): can Redwood Optimize suggest quant for us?
[07:02] Samir (Redwood): yes, that's part of the Optimize toolkit — it will propose int8 vs int4 and expected cost/quality delta. it's advisory; you'll control rollouts.
[07:10] Melissa (Polaris CTO): ok. any compliance gaps we should be aware of for private deployment in our cloud region (eu-west-1)?
[07:17] Jules (Redwood SE): no major gaps — Redwood Private supports EU regions, data residency controls, and you can bring your KMS. we'll include the SOC2/ISO attestations and regional deployment notes.
[07:29] Samir (Redwood): also note we have marketplace listings for certain clouds that can simplify procurement — but procurement/legal may prefer the private contract.
[07:37] Diego (Polaris ML): operational question — will the dedicated pool be shared across Polaris teams? we want per-team isolation.
[07:44] Samir (Redwood): dedicated pools can be partitioned by tenancy; you can create multiple sub-pools per team. that is in the Dedicated product.
[07:53] Aisha (Polaris SRE): for the 48h run, do you need network-level access? or can we replay logs to Redwood?
[07:59] Jules (Redwood SE): replay logs are fine for benchmarking; for end-to-end tests we might ask for a temporary VPC peering during a short window. we'll start with replays.
[08:09] Melissa (Polaris CTO): Diego, can you confirm you'll export prompt traces?
[08:13] Diego (Polaris ML): yes, I'll pull 3 days and anonymize PII and drop them into the secure bucket. expect that by tomorrow.
[08:20] Samir (Redwood): great. I'll send the spreadsheet after the call. Jules, anything else from infra side?
[08:26] Jules (Redwood SE): just a note — we recommend enabling per-route TTL on cache entries to avoid stale personalization. also, on very high-cardinality keys caching hurts more than helps. we'll include heuristics in the doc.
[08:42] Melissa (Polaris CTO): thanks. can you also include a simple cost calculator template so finance can plug numbers in?
[08:48] Samir (Redwood): yes — pricing worksheet and sample calculator will be included.
[08:53] Diego (Polaris ML): are there limits to batch size? we saw context window + batch size interactions cause spikes in memory.
[08:59] Jules (Redwood SE): batch size is dynamic — runtime chooses per-request micro-batches to fit memory. but you can cap max batch size and sequence length to bound memory. we recommend keeping max tokens per batch under the observed GPU memory threshold.
[09:12] Aisha (Polaris SRE): can we get traces for the autoscaler adjustments? we'd like to reproduce the transient backlog.
[09:18] Jules (Redwood SE): yes, we'll export the scheduler logs and share a short RCA in the repo.
[09:24] Melissa (Polaris CTO): ok last thing — what's the timeline to get meaningful numbers we can use in an internal review?
[09:31] Samir (Redwood): plan: you send traces by EOD tomorrow, Jules runs 48h replay starting Monday, we analyze Tuesday and sync Wednesday with a results deck. so roughly 6 business days.
[09:42] Diego (Polaris ML): that works. one more question — any vendor lock-in concerns with Redwood private?
[09:50] Samir (Redwood): deployment artifacts are standard containers and infra as code; artifacts are portable. model versions can be pinned and exported. we try to minimize lock-in but obviously there are optimizations in the runtime.
[10:05] Melissa (Polaris CTO): perfect. let's capture the recap and next steps.
[10:10] Samir (Redwood): recap: 48h benchmark with production prompts, enable prefix caching on target routes, conservative tokens/$ estimate shared, and security + pricing docs delivered. action items assigned. we'll meet same time next Tuesday. Thanks everyone.
[10:28] end of recording
